name: Real-Time Provider Health
brief: Keep routing after the preferred provider goes offline during the run.
context: Provider A starts strong but goes offline. Provider B remains available.
narrative:
The starter policy assumes Provider A is always the best. That works for the first payments, then A goes offline and new attempts fail.

A real routing controller reevaluates live health for every decision. When A is unavailable, it should fall back to B instead of continuing to send work into a broken lane.
objective: Process every payment with at most one failure while provider health changes.
learningObjective: Make a fresh decision from live state instead of committing to one route.
intelligenceExplanation:
The provider cards update as the simulation runs. A is preferred while it is online, but B must take over after the outage.

Place the live availability rules in the correct order and watch the lane status change during the run.
hint: Use WHEN onlineA → route-a above WHEN onlineB → route-b so B takes over after A drops.
hints: Watch Provider A's card — it goes offline partway through the run.
A fixed 'always route A' rule can't adapt. Use a live condition: WHEN onlineA → DO route-a.
Put WHEN onlineB → DO route-b underneath it, so B takes over after A drops.

steps.label: At most one failed payment through the health change

rules.description: Naive: always route to A (breaks when A goes offline).

functions.description: Send the payment through Provider A.
Send the payment through Provider B.
Hold the payment for a tick.

objectives.label: Keep total cost at or below ₦2.00
